thread:
Priya: Quick design review — prototyping a compact p95 row + inline heatmap for the latency dashboard. Dropping the full chart in favor of a denser row. Thoughts on copy, keyboard nav, and sampling controls? :eyes: Alex: Nice direction. Two tiny nits: 1) Label the metric as 'p95 latency (ms)' — we should include units. 2) Tooltip should be explicit: '95th percentile latency (worst 5% of requests)'. Short and clear. Jamie: Agree with Alex. Also noticed the heatmap ramp has low contrast on dark theme; mid-tone bins are barely distinguishable. Failing WCAG for some ranges — we should increase contrast or use patterned fills for low-mid bins. :warning: Luis: Time-range presets dropdown feels a bit heavy in the compact header. What if we replace the dropdown with a segmented control: 1h / 6h / 24h / 7d and a small overflow menu for custom ranges? That helps keyboard users too. Marta: Accessibility checklist: ensure focus outlines on segmented control, aria-labels for each preset, and aria-live for streaming updates on the p95 value. For sampling controls, copy must state state + rate, e.g. 'Sampling: Auto (10%)' so screenreaders relay current mode. Priya: Good call. On sampling copy I'm torn between 'Adaptive sampling' and 'Dynamic sampling'. Which is terser and clearer? Also thinking of a short explainer under the control: 'Adaptive sampling reduces cost while preserving p95 accuracy'. Alex: Prefer 'Adaptive sampling' — shorter and commonly understood. For the explainer, maybe: 'Adaptive sampling preserves tail accuracy while reducing token cost.' Keep it one line. Jamie: Microcopy for p95 tooltip: pick one of these — '95th percentile latency' OR 'Latency below which 95% of requests fall'. I vote '95th percentile latency' for brevity. Luis: Keyboard nav specifics: Left/Right to move between presets, Enter to open custom range, Esc to close. Add aria-keyshortcuts and visible focus ring. I'll add a small spec snippet to the PR. Luis: Snippet for segmented presets (for devs to implement): ```html
``` Marta: Also: ensure colorblind-friendly palette for heatmap. We should run the ramp through a Deuteranopia simulator. If contrast still fails, add a hover pattern or outline at low opacity. DesignBot: Checklist updated — contrast check, keyboard nav, aria labels, tooltip copy. Linked design PR #412 and accessibility ticket ACC-88. Priya: Thanks everyone — I'll update the Figma file and push a small copy + accessibility PR today. If no objections, plan to ship to staging tomorrow morning. :shipit: Marta: +1 :thumbsup: Alex: Looking good, :eyes: — will review the PR later today.
